rows.title: Communications Portal Launch!
rows.message:
Hello Maine DOE Colleagues,

Thank you to everyone who attended the demo today – we are very excited to share the communications portal, which will unify all of our resources into one space. As we launch this to the department, if there is feedback or questions as you get into the space, please let us know.

Below is information on how to access the portal, as well as the recording if you missed the demo (we highly encourage you to watch the demo before accessing the portal).

Recording: Communications Portal Demo.mp4

Portal: https://gateway.maine.gov/doe/communications/index.html - Reminder to not share this URL with external audiences & BOOKMARK!

Password: MaineDOE123!X

Best,

The Communications Team

About the Portal:

____________________________________________________________

WHAT'S INSIDE

Portal sections

The Portal offers easy access to all communication spaces including files, workflow, and expanded information on the following sections:

Homebase

Your landing spot when you open the portal. Everything else is one click away, and this is where you get the daily-driver context: what the team is talking about, what's in the news, how to reach us.

  • About: a plain-English overview of what the portal is and how to use it.
  • Notifications: internal team updates and announcements from Comms.
  • Maine DOE News: the latest from the department's public communications channels.
  • Social: quick links to our social feeds so you can see what's live.
  • Contact: reach the Comms team directly.

Branding & Comms

The interactive Brand Guide. Same content as the PDF in the Handbook, but tabbed, searchable, and always current.

  • Colors, typography, voice, and language, with live examples.
  • Logos and image guidance, including secondary team logos.
  • Correspondence standards: signatures, letterhead, official letters.
  • Resources: the Communications Workflow, SharePoint folders, Handbook, accessibility tools.

EnGiNE

Quick access to Maine's statewide professional learning platform, plus a primer for anyone who wants to build something in it.

  • What you can create: Information Portals, Training, Courses in a Series, Office Hours.
  • Direct links to visit, sign in, create an account, or open the Support Center.
  • The Communications Orientation course for new DOE staff.

Calendar

This is the big change with this launch. You now submit and manage your own DOE PD calendar events directly, in real time. No more emailing Comms and waiting.

  • Submit new events with a guided form: audience, focus area, location, register link, all-day or specific times, recurrence, additional dates.
  • View the live public calendar right inside the portal so you can spot conflicts before you submit.
  • Edit my events: enter your email, pull up every event you've submitted, and edit or cancel with one click.

Publication

A single home for everything the department sends out. Five tabs.

  • Overview: content ownership rules, the materials-at-a-glance list, social media approval checklist, official letter guidance, file-naming conventions.
  • The Commons: a live feed of the latest blog posts, plus the full step-by-step publishing directions in one click.
  • Newsroom: live stats from the WordPress Newsroom (today's views, weekly and monthly totals, top articles, top referrers) and a searchable list of every article published in the last 365 days.
  • Newsletter Builder: our drag-and-drop tool for branded DOE bulletins, with a training video and getting-started guidance.
  • Mailchimp: campaign performance for the established Mailchimp newsletters (open rate, click rate, deliverability).

Templates

Official presentation, letterhead, and design templates for all DOE staff. The versions your team should be using, always current.

  • PowerPoint and other templates in the DOE brand.
  • Word and PDF letterhead templates.
  • Logo variants (color, monochrome, secondary team logos where approved).
  • Design templates for common asks: flyers, one-pagers, social graphics.

YouTube

Submit and track video uploads to the DOE YouTube channel. Everything flows through here so we know what's coming and can coordinate captions, thumbnails, and publish timing.

  • Submit a new video with title, description, audience, and target publish date.
  • Track the status of anything you've submitted.
  • Direct links to the SharePoint upload folders for both the Main Channel and EnGiNE.

Website

Not just for Drupal editors. Anyone in the department can use this section to see how our pages are performing, find files on the site, and flag things that need attention.

  • Analytics dashboard: page views, traffic trends, and top pages across maine.gov/doe.
  • Page stats: dig into any specific page's traffic over the last 30 days.
  • Download stats: which files (PDFs, forms, guides) people are actually pulling down.
  • File manager: browse and search every file uploaded to maine.gov/doe. No Drupal login needed.
  • Page explorer: find any page on the site by title, path, or owner.
  • Request deletion: flag a page or file for removal without going through the full Drupal workflow.
  • Moderation queue: if you're a Drupal editor, see what's pending review.

Comms Files

A one-click jump into the shared Communications SharePoint folder. The portal doesn't recreate SharePoint, it just gets you there faster.

  • Shared team folders, templates, and working assets.
  • Opens in your SharePoint tab so downloads and edits work normally.

Wayfinder

  • Help center to navigate the portal – ask a question to be directed on where you can find info
  • We are still populating the knowledgebase, so if you don’t get an answer – let us know!

rows.title: Admin Back-to-School Backpack Final Review
rows.message:
Hi all,

 

The Back to School Backpack for Administrators is ready for a final look before it goes live, and I'd love your eyes on it.

 

It's a preview node in Drupal, so you'll need to log in first. Head to www.maine.gov/doe/user and sign in with:

Username: preview

Password: MaineDrupal1!

 

Here's the draft page: https://www.maine.gov/doe/node/4775

 

Then open the link above. Please click through the links in your area and flag anything that's broken, points to the wrong place, or needs a wording or content fix. If there's a resource you think is missing, send it over.

 

Thanks to everyone who has sent over revisions thus far -- if you've sent over revisions and you don't see them live here, please ping me! 

 

Thanks!

Matt
